paragraphs: Mia was a member of the animal club at school. At lunch, she took out a small book about sea animals. "Let's play a guessing game," she said. "I tell you what the animal can do and can't do." "Then you must guess which animal it is." Lily, Leo, and May sat next to her and listened.

"This animal can swim, and it can climb on rocks," said Mia. "It can't run, and it can't fly." "It has eight long arms." "Is it a fish?" asked Leo. "No, a fish has no arms," said Mia. "It is an octopus!" said May. "Yes!" said Mia. "Leo's guess was worse than May's, but it was a good try." "An octopus is faster than a crab, but it can't run on land."

Then it was Lily's turn. "This animal can sleep all day," she said. "It can't read a book, and it can't ride a bike." "It can run, but it is a lazy animal today." Everybody looked at Pip, who was asleep under the table. "It is Pip!" said Leo, and he laughed. "Yes," said Lily. "He could run fast this morning, but now he is tired."

At last, Leo gave a new description. "This is not an animal," he said. "It is round, and you can kick it." "You can throw it, but you can't eat it." "Is it a ball?" asked Mia. "Yes, it is!" said Leo. Pip opened one eye when he heard the word. "Woof!" he said, and he stood up. "Now he can run again," said May. The friends laughed and went out to play with him.
